label: A total holder of another that is not totally held in the act by which it holds cannot be lacking
paraphrase: Conclusion, relative first total holder: it is impossible that there be no f, x and r with f totally holding x in r and f not totally held in r. 'Not totally held' is the negation of TotallyHeld, so it covers three cases: f has several co-holders in r (Control part 2 witnesses this case), f is held in r only by things it holds back, or f is not in act in r (the actualizer premise 40fc38ad-2cfe-4da6-8632-137fc5ff9188, not a premise here, excludes the last). f may also be held in other respects. It is not the conclusion that some total holder is unheld in the act by which it holds.
